_comment: Out-of-box 'Standard Support for Incidents' predefined SLA policy — a faithful replica of what Salesforce ITSM seeds when a customer clicks the Incident checkbox under 'Create Predefined Policies' in Setup (Incident process type only). Source of truth for Phase 2-OOB. This is a DATA template, not a ready-to-POST body: substitute <businessHoursId> / <AccountId> at runtime and translate the criteria per the recipe in references/mcp-invocation.md (Predefined Incident Policy). Byte-for-byte modeled on core service-itsm-impl default-sla-policies/incident.json (the resource DefaultSlaServiceImpl reads and seeds) + shared_core_ui_labels/incident-management.xml (DefaultSeededSla): 6 milestones — Critical (30/120) and High (60/240) each Priority Equals, plus a MERGED Moderate-or-Low tier (240/960) whose ACTIVE criterion is a Priority OR (filterLogic '1 OR 2' over two Equals rows, Moderate + Low). NOTE: the core template also carries a per-tier CANCEL criterion, but the public /connect/sla-management route has NO 'CANCEL' milestoneState (valid states: ACTIVE, COMPLETE, PAUSE, UNPAUSE) — so this replica OMITS cancelWhen. The ACTIVE Priority criterion alone gates engagement (an off-tier Incident never matches), making CANCEL redundant. Every milestone uses startTimeBasedOn MILESTONE_CRITERIA (the OOB timer starts when the milestone criteria first match, NOT from the SLA-process created date). WHY REPLICATE INSTEAD OF CALLING THE UI'S OWN API: the checkbox invokes DefaultSlaPolicyController.saveSelectedOptions, an @AuraEnabled controller (core/ui-service-itsm-components) whose only caller of DefaultSlaService.createDefaultSlaPolicies is that Aura action — there is NO public REST/Connect wrapper, so the headless MCP (which dispatches REST/Connect) cannot invoke the seeder directly; it reproduces the seeder's exact output via the public /connect/sla-management routes.

policy.name: Standard Support for Incidents
policy._activeNote: The OOB backend creates the SlaProcess with active:false, then flips it active:true during auto-entitlement activation. When replicating via the public /connect/sla-management/sla-policies POST, create it directly with active:true (same as the custom Phase 2 flow) to avoid the Connect activate PATCH, which can 500 headless.

_milestoneTypesNote: DETECT BEFORE CREATE. Enabling the SLA Management feature pre-seeds a default MilestoneType catalog (commonly First Response, Follow Up, Periodic Update, and Resolve Within). A blind POST for a name that already exists returns HTTP 500 ('already exists') and half-seeds the policy. First read the catalog (SOQL SELECT Id, Name FROM MilestoneType WHERE Name IN ('Acknowledge Within','Resolve Within'), or GET .../milestone-types), reuse any match by id, and POST only the missing name(s). See references/mcp-invocation.md (Predefined Incident Policy, seed step 1).

entitlement._note: The OOB backend auto-creates the Entitlement during activation. When replicating headless, create it via POST /sobjects/Entitlement on the resolved Account (same as the custom Phase 2 flow), SlaProcessId = the seeded policy, backdated StartDate for immediate engagement.
entitlement.name: Standard Support for Incidents

matchAllCriterion._note: The OOB seeds an always-true entitlement criterion so every Incident matches automatically. ATTEMPT to replicate it via POST /connect/sla-management/entitlement-criteria: `describe` the route FIRST and send its exact input fields — it rejects `filterType`, and a wrong body returns a 400 (a wrong-payload error, NOT a platform gap). Only if the create still 400s after using the described schema, fall back to the date-windowed Entitlement alone and REPORT only the engagement-scope consequence: the policy then engages on Incidents wired to this Entitlement (EntitlementId set), not automatically on every Incident. Do NOT tell the user the route is 'unreachable' or 'undiscoverable' — it works; the body just needs its correct fields. The date-windowed Entitlement + the milestone criteria above are still sufficient to engage the Phase 3 test Incident.

_replicationNotes.table: Every criterion filters the Incident table (filterItems[].table = "Incident").
_replicationNotes.activeCriterion: The public Attach-Milestone route's milestoneCriteria carries the ACTIVE criterion — filterType RuleFilter, milestoneState ACTIVE (UPPERCASE — the server matches this case-sensitively; a wrong-case 'Active' returns 201 but silently drops the criterion, collapsing every Incident onto the lowest-order/Critical tier), milestoneAgreementType SLA (customer-facing; OLA is the internal alternative — W-23959162). The priority-tier row IS this active criterion; it is what tiers the policy.
_replicationNotes.completion: The OOB completion (Status In resolved-set) criterion uses milestoneState COMPLETE (UPPERCASE). There is NO CANCEL state on the public route (valid: ACTIVE, COMPLETE, PAUSE, UNPAUSE), so no cancel criterion is sent — the ACTIVE Priority criterion alone gates engagement (matches examples/milestone-patterns.md Pattern 3). Verify tiering by runtime: create a Moderate/Low test Incident and confirm its EntityMilestone lands on the 240/960 tier, not 30/120 (the create response always echoes milestoneCriteria:[] regardless of success, so it cannot confirm persistence).
_replicationNotes.orClause: The core OOB template groups Moderate+Low into ONE tier via an ACTIVE filterLogic '1 OR 2' over two Priority Equals rows (Moderate, Low) — see incident.json orders 5-6. This template mirrors that exactly: orders 5-6 carry activeWhen.filterLogic '1 OR 2' with rows [Priority Equals Moderate, Priority Equals Low]. The public milestone-criteria route accepts this OR via customLogicExpression (the same MilestoneCriteriaInputRepresentation the /connect/sla-management milestones route consumes), so it need NOT be split into separate Equals milestones. Seed 6 milestones as listed. If the live route rejects the OR filterLogic, fall back to two separate Priority Equals milestones (Moderate, Low) with the same timeTriggers — behavior-equivalent. The merged tier has NO cancelWhen, matching the core template (orders 5-6 have ACTIVE + COMPLETE only).
_replicationNotes.statusIn: Status 'In [Resolved, Completed, Closed]' has no single-row In operator, so each completeWhen above is already PRE-SPLIT into a filterLogic ('1 OR 2 OR 3') across three Status Equals rows — the data file never carries a route-rejected In operator. If the route rejects filterLogic, split into one Status Equals row per value (behavior-equivalent). Validate each Status/Priority value against the live Incident picklist before seeding.
_replicationNotes.midTier: Map the mid tier to the org's ACTUAL mid-priority label — 'Moderate' on the standard ITSM picklist, but many orgs label it 'Medium'. In the merged orders 5-6 activeWhen.rows, use whichever label the live Incident.Priority picklist carries in place of 'Moderate' (keep the 'Low' row as-is). Drop a row from the OR only when its value is genuinely absent from the picklist, and note any dropped/relabeled tier in the report.
